name: Tamar Braxton
description:
'''Tamar Estine Braxton''' (born March 17, 1977) is an American singer, songwriter, actress, and television personality. She began her music career as a founding member of the [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] group [[The Braxtons]], formed with her four sisters. The group released its debut [[studio album]], ''[[So Many Ways]]'', in 1996. After pursuing a solo career, Braxton released her debut album, ''[[Tamar (album)|Tamar]]'', through [[DreamWorks Records]] in 2000. Following a hiatus from solo recording, she returned with ''[[Love and War (Tamar Braxton album)|Love and War]]'' (2013), which reached number two on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and topped the ''Billboard'' Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart.

Braxton subsequently released the albums ''[[Calling All Lovers]]'' (2015) and ''[[Bluebird of Happiness (album)|Bluebird of Happiness]]'' (2017), as well as the [[Christmas album]] ''[[Winter Loversland]]'' (2013). In 2025, she released the extended play (EP) ''Heartbreak Retrograde'' and its accompanying film. Her music has earned her four [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] nominations, a [[BET Award]], and three [[Soul Train Music Awards]].

As a television personality, Braxton starred alongside her mother and sisters in the [[We TV]] reality series ''[[Braxton Family Values]]'' (2011–2020) and appeared in the spin-off ''[[Tamar & Vince]]''. She co-hosted the syndicated daytime talk show ''[[The Real (talk show)|The Real]]'' from 2013 to 2016, receiving two [[Daytime Emmy Award]] nominations for her work on the program. In 2019, she won the second season of the American reality competition series ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2 (American season)|Celebrity Big Brother]]'', becoming the first Black winner of the US version of ''[[Big Brother (American TV series)|Big Brother]]''. Her subsequent television work has included hosting ''To Catch a Beautician'', competing on ''Queens Court'' in 2023, and co-starring in the reality series ''[[The Braxtons]]''.

Braxton has also pursued acting in film, television, and theater. Her screen roles include the film ''[[True to the Game (film)#Trilogy|True to the Game 2: Gena's Story]]'' (2020), the series ''[[Kingdom Business]]'' (2022) and the [[animated sitcom]] ''[[Young Love (TV series)|Young Love]]'' (2023).
